evals.prompt: Teach me enough SQL to inspect our analytics data over the next two afternoons. Put the materials in /home/me/learning/sql-pilot. Use the PostgreSQL tutorial and our approved schema guide as sources. I will show understanding by writing and explaining five queries.
evals.expected_output: Creates a bounded SQL learning pilot in the learner-selected workspace. It records the mission, two-afternoon bound, named trusted sources, and five-query explanation evidence plan. It offers short source-cited lessons and practices, then records demonstrated work rather than claiming mastery.
assertions: Records a single observable mission and its bound
Uses the learner-selected five-query evidence plan
Keeps the pilot to a bounded number of lesson and practice cycles
Distinguishes sourced claims from teaching guidance
Does not claim mastery without learner-produced evidence

evals.prompt: Teach me distributed systems. Pick the best sources, make whatever workspace you want, and keep going until I am an expert.
evals.expected_output: Does not start a course. It asks the learner to select a workspace, narrow the mission to an observable bounded outcome, provide trusted sources, and choose learning evidence. It explains that it cannot promise expertise from an unbounded program.
assertions: Declines to infer expertise or run an unbounded program

evals.prompt: What is a SQL JOIN? Give me a short answer with one example.
evals.expected_output: Answers the focused question without creating a teaching workspace, learning mission, record, or multi-session program. It may offer the teaching skill only if the user later wants a bounded learning mission.
assertions: Does not create a workspace or learning record
Does not require a multi-session mission for a short answer
